input.question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?
input.ground_truth: It’s just tradition at this point. At one point in history encores were real but now every band just does it because it’s the thing every other band does. There are exceptions though, I’ve seen Bad Religion headline numerous times going through a 25-30 song set and just end it with no encore. The Supersuckers announce its time for “the fake encore” about 3 songs from the end...

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do bands do planned encores at concerts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friends are putting on a show for your family. You sing some songs, and everyone cheers and claps. Then, you all go behind the curtain (or hide behind the sofa!). But your family is still excited and wants more music! So, you come back out and sing a few more songs just for them. That’s called an encore.

Bands do planned encores because they want to make their fans super happy and give them a special surprise at the end of the concert. It’s like a bonus treat! Also, it’s a fun tradition—fans know to keep cheering because there might be more music coming. So, the band plans it ahead of time to make the concert even more exciting!
